title: HKMA Announces New Phase of Project Ensemble for Tokenised Deposits and Digital Assets
summary: On 13 November 2025, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) announced a new phase of Project Ensemble -- HKMA's ongoing initiative piloting tokenisation and settlement infrastructure for Hong Kong's financial markets -- describing the new phase's purpose, per the press release's own title, as supporting 'real-value transactions in tokenised deposits and digital assets.' A tokenised deposit is a bank deposit represented as a transferable digital token rather than only as an entry in a bank's internal ledger. HKMA's press-release page returned no retrievable content on every attempt made during this review, so which institutions are participating, the new phase's specific scope beyond the title's own wording, and any stated timeline are not confirmed against primary source text; this summary reflects only the announcement's own published title.
why_it_matters: Project Ensemble is how HKMA tests new settlement infrastructure for tokenised money before it reaches the broader market, so a new phase signals the initiative moving toward the next stage of real transactions rather than only simulated ones. For a newcomer, it shows Hong Kong's central-banking-style regulator actively building infrastructure for tokenised finance, alongside its separate licensing regimes for stablecoins and exchanges.
